cover_lines: Q3 sales climb as unsold stock builds
Blue Line, Pink Line and suburban rail
cover.headline: Bengaluru Builds Out: Rail, Roads and Townships
cover.subhead: Sales are recovering, launches are heavy and infrastructure timelines keep shifting. What it means for buyers across the city and its fast-growing edges.

editor_note.text: The latest quarter brought a firmer market. According to ANAROCK, Bengaluru housing sales rose 12% YoY to 16,670 units in Q3 2026. The agency also says MMR and Bengaluru together accounted for 48% of total sales across the seven cities it tracks, a reminder of how much national demand now rests on these two markets.

Jobs continue to underpin that demand. Colliers says Bengaluru led Jan-Sep 2026 office leasing at 15.7 million sq ft, driven partly by GCCs and flex operators. ANAROCK adds that GCCs made up 70% of the roughly 10.8 million sq ft of office absorption in H1 2026. Where offices cluster, housing follows.

Infrastructure is the other half of the story, and timelines deserve a careful read. BMRCL's Blue Line has reached 72% overall construction progress, per Business Today, yet Construction World reports the full opening has slipped to March 2028. K-RIDE says it is committed to starting suburban rail operations by December 2028. Buy for today's connectivity, not tomorrow's.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line (KR Puram–Silk Board, Phase 2A)
insights.title: Construction World reported on 28 October 2026 that trial runs on the 19.75-km KR Puram–Central Silk Board stretch of the Blue Line (Outer Ring Road) were expected to begin by the end of October, with services targeted for mid-2027 subject to statutory clearances. No source found confirms trials started.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line (KR Puram–Silk Board)
insights.title: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said station entry and exit works on the KR Puram–Silk Board Blue Line stretch had reached 88 per cent completion (Construction World, 28 Oct 2026).

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated section
insights.title: Construction World reported on 28 October 2026 that approval for passenger operations on the Pink Line's elevated section (Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere) was expected within four to five days, with the state having written to the Union government seeking an early inauguration date.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line KR Puram–Central Silk Board
insights.title: Construction World reported on 28 October that trial runs on Namma Metro's 19.75-km KR Puram–Central Silk Board (Blue Line) stretch were expected to begin by the end of October, with construction 87% complete and services targeted by mid-2027.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line KR Puram–Central Silk Board
insights.title: Construction World on 28 October reported overall construction of the KR Puram–Silk Board Blue Line at 87 per cent, with services targeted to begin by mid-2027 subject to statutory clearances.

insights.subject: Pink Line elevated stretch Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere
insights.title: The 7.5 km elevated Pink Line stretch between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere received safety clearance from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (Southern Circle) on Wednesday 28 October, Oneindia reported on 29 October.

insights.subject: Pink Line inauguration
insights.title: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said Prime Minister Narendra Modi would visit Bengaluru on 15 November and was likely to inaugurate the Pink Line elevated stretch; the date was still awaiting confirmation from the Centre.

insights.subject: Pink Line elevated stretch opening
insights.title: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said in a post on X that the Pink Line stretch was 'ready for public service' and that the state had asked the Centre for an inauguration date; he indicated opening by mid-November.

insights.subject: Purple Line disruption at Indiranagar
insights.title: On 30 October a passenger entered the tracks at Indiranagar station around 9:22 am, delaying Purple Line services about 10 minutes; the passenger was rescued and services were normal by 9:40 am, with some Green Line trains held at Majestic.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line (Phase 2A) KR Puram–Central Silk Board
insights.title: Construction World reported on 28 October 2026 that trial runs on Namma Metro's 19.75-km KR Puram–Central Silk Board Blue Line stretch were expected to begin by the end of October, with overall construction 87% complete. Services are targeted for mid-2027, subject to statutory clearances.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line Phase 2A delay
insights.title: Construction World on 28 October 2026 reported that the full Blue Line corridor up to Central Silk Board is scheduled to be ready by the middle of next year. The minister said the project was already delayed by a year, and officials blamed Cauvery water pipelines, drainage lines and traffic.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated section Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere
insights.title: Construction World on 28 October 2026 reported that operational clearance for the Pink Line's 7.5-km elevated section was expected within four to five days. The state had asked for an early inauguration but had not received a confirmed date.
